newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank injects T$8.25 bln in funds.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank injects T$8.25 bln in funds.

text.p: Taiwan's central bank, reacting as money rates bubbled ever higher, on Friday injected T$8.25 billion worth of funds into the banking system through open market operations, a central bank official said.

The bank, contacted directly by interested financial institutions, purchased back T$8.25 billion in negotiable certificates of deposit offered by financial institutions with a single yield at 9.0 percent, the official said.
The institutions have the option of repurchasing the instruments within seven days of their issue, the official said.
Taiwan's overnight interbank rate closed higher for the ninth consecutive session on Thursday to reach a 21-month peak of 8.957 percent and rocketed into double digits on Friday.
The rate stood at 10.732 percent shortly before close on Friday, with large amount of funds leaving the banking system and streaming into the recently red hot stock market.
The central bank said it would continue to watch closely the banking system's liquidity flow.
